newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest crops survive entry of cold system.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest crops survive entry of cold system.

text.p: A cool weather system entered the western U.S. Midwest overnight, but there was no widespread frost, meteorologists said.

Temperatures dipped into the mid- to high-30s degrees Fahrenheit area early Tuesday across eastern South Dakota, eastern Nebraska and northwest Iowa. Spencer, Iowa, in the northwest portion of the state, reported a low of 33 degrees.
"Most likely there was scattered frost in that region," Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist, said of the area near Spencer.
The cold should move eastward dropping temperatures into the mid 30s across southeast Minnesota, northeast Iowa, southern Wisconsin and possibly northwest Illinois.
"A little more frost is possible tomorrow (Wednesday) morning," said Burgio.
Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis said there is a minor threat of frost in the western Midwest and "virtually no threat" in the eastern Midwest.
Rain and cloudy conditions forecast for this week should lessen the chance of frost late this week when a second cold system was due in the Midwest, Davis said.
"Lows on Thursday morning will be 43 to 53 across the belt. The mild temps will continue through Saturday. Obviously, there is no threat of any damaging cold during the next five days," Davis said.

Rain on Monday further delayed winter wheat planting from Nebraska to Texas and delayed corn harvest in the southern Midwest. Missouri received 0.50 to 2.0 inches of rain Monday, with greater amounts in isolated areas.
Burgio said he expects rain amounts of 0.5 to 1.5 inches Wednesday and Thursday from southern Kansas to Texas, with scattered showers Tuesday in Colorado, northwest Kansas and Nebraska.
